solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Drawing blood, lymph too, busy nurses conclude job at last (10)

indicatorNotes.busy: busy letters are all over the place
indicatorNotes.nurses: the anagram holds the other letters as a nurse holds a patient
indicatorNotes.at last: take the final letter of each word

blocks.note: last letters of concludE and joB, held inside the anagram

annotation.surface: A hospital phlebotomist at the end of a busy shift, finishing off one last blood sample.
annotation.walkthrough: The anagram of LYMPH TOO gives PHL…OTOMY with a gap; EB fills it. 'Drawing blood' reads as part of the scene but is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Phlebotomy is the medical term for drawing blood from a vein.

entries.clue: Principal ingredient in parkin, brownie and bread (4)

indicatorNotes.Principal ingredient in: the principal, or first, letter of the word

blocks.note: a brownie is a household sprite, like an elf

annotation.surface: A baking recipe: parkin, brownies and bread, and what goes into them.
annotation.walkthrough: Parkin is a sticky ginger cake from northern England. 'Brownie' and 'bread' both pretend to be baking; one is a sprite, the other slang for money.
annotation.definitionFit: Pelf is money, usually ill-gotten, and bread is slang for money.

entries.clue: Dwelt on shattering disappointment (3-4)

indicatorNotes.shattering: the letters are broken up and rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone brooding over a crushing disappointment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shattering' reads as an adjective on disappointment, but it is the instruction to break up DWELT ON.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: being let down by someone is being disappointed, and the hyphenated noun names the event.

entries.clue: Oily fish — massive, skinless and spiky (13)

indicatorNotes.skinless: the word loses its outer letters, its skin

blocks.note: GIANT without its outer letters G and T

annotation.surface: A description of some huge, prickly, oily fish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oily fish' looks like one phrase; the definition is only 'Oily', and fish is the first piece. Brilliantine is a hair oil, so brilliantined hair is slicked with it.
annotation.definitionFit: Brilliantined hair has been dressed with brilliantine, a hair oil, so it is oily.

entries.clue: Some important Rastafarian religious writings (6)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters in the words that follow

annotation.surface: Scriptures that matter to a Rastafarian.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rastafarian setting points toward the Bible, but the tantras are Hindu and Buddhist texts; the answer is simply sitting inside the words.
annotation.definitionFit: The tantras are a body of Hindu and Buddhist religious texts.

entries.clue: Flower Gloria cultivated in Maryland (8)

indicatorNotes.cultivated: the letters are worked over like soil
indicatorNotes.in: the anagram goes inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: MD is the postal abbreviation for Maryland; this is its first half

annotation.surface: A gardener named Gloria growing flowers in Maryland.
annotation.walkthrough: MD is the US state abbreviation for Maryland. 'Flower' and 'cultivated' make a gardening scene, but only 'cultivated' is working as a mixing instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the orange-flowered marigold is one particular flower.

entries.clue: Mums dropping others like hot potatoes (4)

indicatorNotes.dropping: OTHERS is dropped from the word

blocks.note: H = hot, as on a tap

annotation.surface: Mothers dropping everyone else like a hot potato.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Like hot potatoes' is an idiom the eye reads as one phrase; it splits into AS, H and the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: mash is short for mashed potato, as in 'bangers and mash', so potatoes stands for it directly.

entries.clue: Boxer intended to give up a foodstuff (7)

indicatorNotes.to give up: the word gives up one of its letters, the A that follows

annotation.surface: A boxer meant to give up some item of his diet.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'a' does double duty in the surface as an article, but in the wordplay it is the letter MEANT loses.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal, rather old word: from Latin alere, to nourish, it names anything that feeds, the same root as alimentary canal.

entries.clue: Agony and ecstasy interrupting stag weekend? (10)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: the letter breaks into the middle of the word

blocks.note: a hart is a male deer, a stag
E = the drug ecstasy; it goes inside HART

annotation.surface: A stag weekend, bachelor party, gone wrong with drugs and misery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stag weekend' reads as the British bachelor party but splits into two pieces: the deer and a short holiday.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the grief of a broken heart is a mental anguish, which is what agony means here.

entries.clue: Terribly valiant Northern European (7)

indicatorNotes.Terribly: the letters are in a terrible state

annotation.surface: Praise for a very brave person from the north of Europe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terribly valiant' reads as 'extremely brave'; terribly is the instruction to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: A Latvian comes from Latvia, a Baltic country in northern Europe.

entries.clue: Model of democracy disheartened leader in Africa (7)

indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart, the middle letters, is taken out
indicatorNotes.leader in: the first letter of the word

annotation.surface: An African leader held up as a model of democracy, but demoralised.
annotation.walkthrough: A republic is a democracy; REPUBLIC has eight letters, so its heart is the middle pair UB. 'Model' reads as an adjective in the surface but is the noun definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the noun sense: a scale model of a ship or building is an exact copy of it.

entries.clue: Travel bug ultimately stops Pierre running country (13)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the final letter of the word
indicatorNotes.stops: the letter plugs a gap in the anagram, like a stopper
indicatorNotes.running: running means on the move, so the letters of Pierre will not stay where they stand

blocks.note: first part of PIERRE rearranged as PERERI
last letter of bug, plugged into the anagram

annotation.surface: A Frenchman's wanderlust finally cut short while he runs a country.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Travel bug' reads as wanderlust, but 'bug' belongs to the wordplay and only 'Travel' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Peregrination is a long journey, travelling from place to place.

entries.clue: Very, very good flag (5,5)

blocks.note: roger = message received, understood: very good

annotation.surface: An enthusiastic judgement on a flag: really excellent.
annotation.walkthrough: Jolly as an adverb meaning very is British informal. Roger is the radio reply meaning 'received and understood', which does the job of 'very good!' as a reply.
annotation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the pirates' skull-and-crossbones flag.

entries.clue: Firstly elicit admission, then scoff (3)

indicatorNotes.Firstly: take the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of Elicit Admission Then

annotation.surface: An interrogator extracting a confession, then sneering at it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' in the surface means to mock; the definition uses its other sense, to eat greedily.
annotation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it quickly and greedily.

entries.clue: Delivery of cast at fault in every part (10)

indicatorNotes.Delivery of: the word as it is delivered in speech

blocks.note: out = wrong, mistaken, as in 'your figures are out'

annotation.surface: A theatre production where every cast member fluffs their lines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' and 'cast' look like theatre words; cast is the past-tense verb, and delivery is how the word is spoken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a house painted throughout has every part painted.

entries.clue: House of Lancaster? (6)

blocks.note: the surface wants a royal house, a dynasty; the setter means a building that houses something
not the medieval kings but the Avro Lancaster, an RAF bomber of the Second World War

annotation.surface: The royal House of Lancaster, the line of English kings.
annotation.walkthrough: The House of Lancaster is a line of medieval English kings; the Lancaster here is the Second World War RAF bomber, and its house is a hangar.
annotation.definitionFit: A hangar is the building that houses an aircraft such as a Lancaster.

entries.clue: Fellow Christian’s senior officer and better half (8)

indicatorNotes.half: half of a word is one of its two halves, here the back three letters of the six

blocks.note: Captain Bligh commanded Fletcher Christian on the Bounty

annotation.surface: A churchgoer's commanding officer and his wife.
annotation.walkthrough: Fletcher Christian led the mutiny on the Bounty against Captain Bligh. 'Better half' wants to be a spouse; it is half of the word BETTER. Blighter is British slang for a man.
annotation.definitionFit: A blighter is British informal for a fellow, often a rascal.

entries.clue: Successive boundaries eluding Australian, joint run scorer (8)

indicatorNotes.Successive boundaries eluding: the boundary, or end letter, of each of the next two words slips away

blocks.note: BRUCE, the stock Australian name, without its last letter

annotation.surface: A cricket report: an Australian batsman sharing a run-scoring partnership, with boundaries getting past a fielder.
annotation.walkthrough: Every Australian is 'Bruce' in a well-known Monty Python sketch. A boundary in cricket is a hit to the edge of the field, but here it is the edge of a word. The scorer is a composer.
annotation.definitionFit: Anton Bruckner was an Austrian composer, someone who writes musical scores.

entries.clue: Music is Open University subject (8)

blocks.note: RE = religious education, a school subject

annotation.surface: Music as a course offered by the Open University, Britain's distance-learning university.
annotation.walkthrough: The Open University is a real British institution, so 'Open University' reads as one name; it splits into OVERT and U.
annotation.definitionFit: An overture is an orchestral piece of music that opens an opera or concert.

entries.clue: Starts to etch motif on flat board (7)

indicatorNotes.Starts to: the starting letters of the words that follow

blocks.note: a plane is a flat surface

annotation.surface: A craftsman beginning to engrave a design on a flat wooden board.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flat board' reads as a plank of wood; board is the verb, to get on an aircraft.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: em- means 'put into', so to emplane is to get into a plane, to board it.

entries.clue: Travelling west in Navarre, I spot mountains (6)

indicatorNotes.Travelling west: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left
indicatorNotes.in: the letters sit inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A traveller heading west through Navarre, in northern Spain, sighting mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: Navarre is a region of northern Spain in the Pyrenees, which suits the Spanish word for a mountain range.
annotation.definitionFit: A sierra is a range of jagged mountains, especially in Spain or the Americas.

entries.clue: Audibly moved, spoke from memory (7)

indicatorNotes.Audibly: the answer is how the word sounds

blocks.note: resited = moved to a new site

annotation.surface: Someone visibly emotional reciting from memory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audibly moved' reads as audibly emotional; moved here means relocated, RESITED.
annotation.definitionFit: To recite is to say aloud from memory.

entries.clue: Quiet American added to my collection of texts (6)

annotation.surface: A reserved American contributing to someone's library.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive; it is the exclamation, like British 'cor!'. Cor is a British expression of surprise.
annotation.definitionFit: Latin for body: a body of writing, such as all of one author's works, is the whole collection of texts.

entries.clue: Hiatus hernia finally checked by doctor (3)

indicatorNotes.finally: the final letter of the word

blocks.note: GP = general practitioner, a doctor; first half
last letter of hernia, held inside GP

annotation.surface: A hiatus hernia being examined by a doctor.
annotation.walkthrough: A hiatus hernia is a real medical condition, so 'Hiatus hernia' reads as one term; hiatus is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: hiatus is Latin for an opening, and in English it means a break or opening in a sequence.

entries.clue: Centre of Birmingham about to be entertained by gypsy magic (10)

indicatorNotes.to be entertained by: the letter is taken in as a guest

blocks.note: the National Exhibition Centre, near Birmingham

annotation.surface: A fortune teller's magic show at a venue in the middle of Birmingham.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Centre of Birmingham' looks like a request for the middle letters; it is the NEC, a big exhibition and concert venue near Birmingham.
annotation.definitionFit: Necromancy is magic, especially communicating with the dead.

entries.clue: Raptor dropping bone for raven (4)

indicatorNotes.dropping: the bone is dropped from the bird

blocks.note: OSPREY without OS, Latin for bone

annotation.surface: A bird of prey letting go of a bone to go after a raven instead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raven' reads as the bird; it is the verb, to hunt and devour.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare verb sense: to raven means to hunt and devour greedily, the root of ravenous, and the bird is not involved.

entries.clue: Old Spanish gentleman tailing grandma relentlessly (2,3,2)

blocks.note: Don is a Spanish title for a gentleman

annotation.surface: An elderly Spanish gentleman following a grandmother everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: The Spanish gentleman appears first in the clue but goes last, because he is tailing NAN.
annotation.definitionFit: On and on means continuing without stopping, relentlessly.

entries.clue: Dog lead (7)

blocks.note: a breed of gun dog that stands still and aims its nose at game
lead as a noun: a hint or tip that sends you in the right direction

annotation.surface: A dog lead, the leash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dog lead' reads as a leash; lead is a noun meaning a clue or hint.
annotation.definitionFit: A pointer is a breed of gun dog, and also a tip or lead.

entries.clue: Kicked rat escaping from trap (4)

indicatorNotes.escaping from trap: trap is slang for mouth, so what escapes it is spoken

blocks.note: a toad, like a rat, is a contemptible person

annotation.surface: Someone booting a rat that was trying to get out of a trap.
annotation.walkthrough: Trap is British slang for mouth ('shut your trap'). The rat is a nasty person, a toad.
annotation.definitionFit: To toe something is to kick it with the toe.

entries.clue: Modern Christmas? (7-3)

blocks.note: belonging to the current era, of now
whimsically, the day on which gifts are given; the question mark flags the pun

annotation.surface: A question about what Christmas is like these days.
annotation.walkthrough: Christmas, the day of giving presents, is whimsically a 'present day', which in the ordinary sense means modern.
annotation.definitionFit: Present-day means belonging to the current era, modern.
